title: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
abstract: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.
summary: This theoretical paper proves a general factorized formula for the determinant associated with a basis of monomials in a commutative semisimple algebra defined by a degeneracy graph. The proof is highly technical, relying on graph analogues of Newton polynomials and establishing a block triangular structure for the evaluation matrix. The result connects algebraic properties to combinatorial invariants, specifically overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove a factorized formula for the determinant of an evaluation matrix associated with a basis of monomials in a commutative semisimple algebra (CASS). This relates the algebraic structure defined by a degeneracy graph to a concrete determinant formula.
main_result: The conjectured factorized formula for the determinant is proven for any number of generators, and the structure of the determinant is shown to be governed by the overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the graph nodes.
method: The proof utilizes graph analogues of Newton polynomials and establishes that the evaluation matrix is block triangular through strategic reordering of rows and columns. The final result is obtained via induction on the number of layers.
model_or_system: The context is a general CASS algebra generated by operators $C_1, \dots, C_L$, which arises in physical settings like the study of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory (AdS/CFT) or Walled Brauer algebras. The structure is encoded by a 'degeneracy graph.'
key_observables: The determinant of the evaluation matrix, which is conjectured and then proven to follow a product formula related to Young diagram overlap volumes.
important_parameters: The number of generators ($L$), the structure of the degeneracy graph, and the eigenvalues associated with the graph nodes.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on the ability to transform the evaluation matrix into a block triangular form via specific row/column permutations, and the initial conjecture regarding the determinant's factorized form.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the graph structure ($\Gamma$), showing nodes, parents, and children, and the mathematical constructions of the graph Newton polynomials and the resulting block-triangular matrix structure.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the basis property of the graph monomials, introduces graph analogues of Newton polynomials, proves the determinant formula using induction on the graph layers, and finally derives the explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the connection between algebraic structures (CASS), graph theory, and combinatorial objects (Young diagrams) provides powerful mathematical tools applicable to quantum field theory and representation theory, which underpins many advanced quantum physics models.
